answer: A beacon-anchored endorsement web resists sybils by making trust scarce and traceable. A newcomer joins only when an established beacon publicly vouches for it, posting a saffron bond slashed if the newcomer proves a clone. Trust then spreads like a ripple: each endorsement hop halves the weight, so one beacon sponsors only a small neighbourhood and distant clones carry near-zero standing. An attacker wanting a hundred fakes must pay a hundred bonds and find a hundred distinct beacon paths, while the public endorsement graph exposes star-shaped clusters for anyone to audit and prune.
